title: The School Science Fair
intro: Reading comprehension: read the diary, then answer 10 questions.

P1.title: The School Science Fair
P1.text:
Thursday, 12 March

Today was the science fair at our school in Sharjah. I was very nervous because it was my first time, and my hands were shaking. My project was a volcano. Before the judges arrived, my friend Hamdan helped me put red paint inside it.

At ten o'clock, the judges walked to our table. I poured vinegar into the volcano, and red bubbles ran down the sides. Everyone clapped! The judges said my volcano was bigger than the others.

Then I looked at the other projects. Layla made a tiny garden that grew inside a glass jar. I think her project was the most beautiful of all. Rashid's robot stopped working after five minutes, which was sad. In my opinion, it needed a stronger battery.

After lunch, the teacher gave out the prizes. I won second place, and Layla won first place. I felt a little disappointed because I wanted to win, but I was proud of my volcano. Next year, I will try again!

questions.prompt: What is the text mainly about?
options: A day at a school science fair
A garden inside a glass jar
A robot that needs a battery
questions.explanation: Every paragraph is about the writer's day at the science fair. The volcano, the garden and the robot are only parts of the day.

questions.prompt: Choose the best meaning for the word from the text.
questions.explanation: The writer says 'it was my first time, and my hands were shaking' - these clues show a worried, afraid feeling.

questions.prompt: At what time did the judges walk to the writer's table?
questions.explanation: Paragraph 2 says: 'At ten o'clock, the judges walked to our table.'

questions.prompt: Choose the best meaning for the word from the text.
questions.explanation: The garden grew 'inside a glass jar', so it must be very small.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is the writer's opinion?
options: I think her project was the most beautiful of all.
Rashid's robot stopped working after five minutes.
The judges walked to our table at ten o'clock.
questions.explanation: 'I think' and 'most beautiful' show what the writer feels. The other sentences tell us things that happened (facts).

questions.prompt: True or false? *Rashid's robot worked for one hour.*
questions.explanation: The text says the robot 'stopped working after five minutes', not one hour.

questions.prompt: What is the writer's opinion about Rashid's robot?
options: It stopped working after five minutes.
It was too big for the table.
questions.explanation: 'In my opinion, it needed a stronger battery.' Stopping after five minutes is a fact, not an opinion.

questions.prompt: 'I felt a little **disappointed** because I wanted to win.' What does *disappointed* mean?
options: a little sad because you wanted something better
questions.explanation: The writer wanted to win but came second, so disappointed means a little sad that things were not as good as hoped.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is a fact, not an opinion?
options: I think her project was the most beautiful of all.
In my opinion, it needed a stronger battery.
questions.explanation: 'I won second place' really happened and can be checked. The other sentences show what the writer thinks or feels.

questions.prompt: Put the events in the order they happened.
items: Hamdan helped put red paint in the volcano.
The judges walked to the table.
Red bubbles ran down the volcano.
The teacher gave out the prizes.
questions.explanation: Before the judges arrived (paint) → at ten o'clock (judges came) → vinegar and bubbles → after lunch (prizes).

Emerging.descriptor: Demonstrates limited understanding of specific information and detail in a short, simple text.
Emerging.feedback: Finds a detail only when the question uses the very same words as the text; may mix up what is true and false.
Emerging.feedforward: Underline the key word in the question, then find the same word in the text.

Developing.descriptor: Demonstrates developing understanding of specific information and detail in a short text.
Developing.feedback: Finds some details but sometimes picks an answer from the wrong paragraph or misses the order of events.
Developing.feedforward: Read the sentence before and after the key word. Number the events as you read.

Meets Expectations.descriptor: Demonstrates an appropriate understanding of most specific information in short, simple texts.
Meets Expectations.feedback: Finds most details and the main idea; true/false and time-order questions still cause some mistakes.
Meets Expectations.feedforward: For true/false, find the exact sentence and check every word, such as five minutes, not one hour.

Secure.descriptor: Demonstrates secure understanding and accurate recall of specific information and detail.
Secure.feedback: Finds details quickly, follows the order of events and understands the main idea of the text.
Secure.feedforward: Tell a partner how you found each answer, using words like before, then and after.

Exceeding.descriptor: Demonstrates confident, accurate and flexible understanding of detail in short texts.
Exceeding.feedback: Consistently finds the right detail and sees how the parts of the text fit together.
Exceeding.feedforward: Write three questions of your own about the diary for a partner to answer.

Emerging.descriptor: Demonstrates limited ability to deduce meaning from context.
Emerging.feedback: Guesses new words without using the words around them, often picking a word that sounds similar.
Emerging.feedforward: Read the whole sentence and ask: what would make sense here?

Developing.descriptor: Demonstrates developing ability to deduce meaning from context.
Developing.feedback: Works out some meanings, usually when the clue is right next to the word.
Developing.feedforward: Look before and after the word for clues, like 'hands were shaking' for nervous.

Meets Expectations.descriptor: Demonstrates an appropriate ability to deduce meaning from context in short texts.
Meets Expectations.feedback: Works out most meanings but can be misled by a feeling word that fits only part of the sentence.
Meets Expectations.feedforward: Put your meaning in place of the word and read the sentence again. Does it still make sense?

Secure.descriptor: Demonstrates secure and accurate deduction of meaning from context.
Secure.feedback: Uses clues in the text to work out new words accurately.
Secure.feedforward: Keep a word log: write the new word, its meaning and the clue that helped you.

Exceeding.descriptor: Demonstrates confident, accurate and flexible deduction of meaning from context.
Exceeding.feedback: Consistently works out meanings and can explain which clues helped.
Exceeding.feedforward: Find another word for each new word (tiny = very small) and use it in a sentence of your own.

Emerging.descriptor: Demonstrates limited recognition of the writer's opinions in a short, simple text.
Emerging.feedback: Often chooses a fact as the opinion, because it is in the text, and does not notice opinion words.
Emerging.feedforward: A fact can be checked. An opinion is what someone thinks or feels. Look for 'I think'.

Developing.descriptor: Demonstrates developing recognition of the writer's opinions in a short text.
Developing.feedback: Spots opinions that start with 'I think' but misses ones without those words.
Developing.feedforward: Look for feeling words like beautiful, sad and best. They often show an opinion.

Meets Expectations.descriptor: Demonstrates an appropriate recognition of the writer's opinions in short, simple texts.
Meets Expectations.feedback: Finds most opinions but can be tricked by a fact that sounds important.
Meets Expectations.feedforward: Ask: could I check this? If yes, it is a fact. If it is a feeling or a view, it is an opinion.

Secure.descriptor: Demonstrates secure and accurate recognition of the writer's opinions.
Secure.feedback: Tells facts from opinions accurately, including opinions without 'I think'.
Secure.feedforward: Find one fact and one opinion in a short text and explain how you know.

Exceeding.descriptor: Demonstrates confident, accurate and flexible recognition of the writer's opinions.
Exceeding.feedback: Consistently separates facts from opinions and explains the clues the writer uses.
Exceeding.feedforward: Rewrite three facts from the diary as opinions, then swap with a partner to check.
